But it invokes the private add_impl directly and compares its result to the same addition expression used by the implementation; that makes it strong as a regression guard for this exact implementation but limited as evidence for the public semantic contract. Pre-refinement review. Kani 0.67 verified this harness successfully: 242 VCCs, zero failures; its caller-location and foreign-function paths were proven unreachable. The harness uses real Box operations with arbitrary i32 values, exact read/write assertions, and a non-Copy drop witness, so it is a sound focused regression guard. Its lifecycle assertion only checked final Box destruction, however: it did not make destruction of a displaced pointee observable when assigning through DerefMut. The registered evidence is Box<i32>, while the lifecycle scenario necessarily uses Box<DropWitness>, so it is supporting behavioral evidence rather than a fully parametric Box proof. Strengthen by replacing a drop-instrumented pointee, asserting one destruction at replacement and a second only at final Box drop. Raw ownership-transfer APIs remain intentionally out of scope under the no-unsafe policy.

Post-refinement review. The requested lifecycle case is now explicit: replacing the boxed DropWitness through DerefMut must advance the shared count from zero to one, and dropping the Box must advance it to two. The exact harness passed Kani 0.67 with 251 checks, zero failures, and two unreachable checks under the native three-minute harness timeout. This is acceptable evidence for the deliberately scoped Box<i32> dereference/write contract plus destructor behavior. It is not a parametric proof for all T and does not cover raw-pointer ownership transfer or allocator-specific behavior; those are separate claims, with raw APIs outside the repository no-unsafe policy.

Pre-refinement review. Kani 0.67 verified the baseline harness successfully with 1,422 checks, zero failures, and 79 unreachable checks under the native three-minute harness timeout. Strengthen with an Ord-compatible drop witness, consume one element, drop that element, then drop Drain and assert that the two remaining values are each dropped and the heap is empty.

The drop witness proves that one yielded value is transferred to its caller, then dropping an unfinished Drain destroys the two remaining values and leaves the heap empty.
